panels.caption: The nine core types and the four lifecycle operations every optimizer must support identically. Algorithm-specific data rides in extension maps.
notes: A checkpoint validates its own digest on load; a mismatch is an error, not a warning.
An optimizer advertises only the actions it genuinely supports — MAPO, for example, declares merge and discard unsupported rather than faking them.

notes: Sealed evaluation splits are fixed before any policy sees a trajectory.

subtitle: One versioned contract for observation, action, transition, reward, checkpoint, pause, fork and single-step — plus the surface a proposer policy would train on.
title: Shared optimizer environment and training loop
verdict: Implemented and exercised by MAPO; not yet mapped onto the other four.
why: MAPO implements the full contract — actions, digests, checkpoint, pause/restart, fork, one-step and trajectory export — and its gates pass. No other optimizer has been mapped onto it yet, so portability is asserted, not shown.
